points.description: States that a stack is a data structure (stores elements) where the last item added is the first removed (last-in-first-out / LIFO), in any wording.
points.partial_credit: Award 2–3 marks if only a related half is given, e.g. says it is a data structure that stores items, or mentions push/pop or adding/removing at one end, without clearly stating last-in-first-out.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating the core idea of last-in-first-out (last added is removed first) in any wording, even brief or informal, e.g. "LIFO structure". Part marks if the answer only says it is a data structure holding items or describes push/pop at one end without the LIFO ordering. No marks for answers that are unrelated or describe first-in-first-out (a queue); extra correct detail is fine.
